'''Rochus Eugen (Robbie) Vogt''' (born December 21, 1929) is a German-American physicist, famous as the director and principal investigator of the [[LIGO]] project from 1987 to 1994.<ref name=breakthrough.caltech>{{cite web|title=New Fellowship Honors Robbie Vogt, Who Shaped World-Leading Observatories|date=June 11, 2019|website=Break Through: The Caltech Campaign|url=https://breakthrough.caltech.edu/vogt_fellowship/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190908220715/https://breakthrough.caltech.edu/vogt_fellowship/ |archive-date=8 September 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Biography==
Vogt studied from 1950 to 1952 at the [[University of Karlsruhe]] and from 1952 to 1953 at [[Heidelberg University]]. In 1953, he came to the [[United States]]. He graduated from the [[University of Chicago]] in physics with a master's degree in 1957 and a PhD in 1961.<ref name=AlumniAward>{{cite news|title=Alumni Award. Rochus "Robbie" Vogt|newspaper=University of Chicago News|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/university-honors-alumni-exceptional-professional-achievements}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation ''Primary cosmic-ray and solar protons''<ref>{{cite thesis|last=Vogt| first= Rochus|year=1961|title=Primary cosmic-ray and solar protons|institution= University of Chicago|degree=PhD| oclc=49433913 |url=https://catalog.lib.uchicago.edu/vufind/Record/4138009}}</ref> was supervised by [[Peter Meyer (astrophysicist)|Peter Meyer]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Müller, Dietrich|title=Peter Meyer (1920–2002)|journal=Bulletin of the American Astronomical Society|date=31 December 2002 |volume=34 |issue=4 |url=https://baas.aas.org/pub/peter-meyer-1920-2002/release/1}}</ref> At [[Caltech]], Vogt was an assistant professor from 1962 to 1965, an associate professor from 1965 to 1970, a full professor from 1970 to 1982, and R. Stanton Avery Distinguished Service from 1982 to 2002, when he retired as professor emeritus. He was chair of Caltech's Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy from 1978 to 1983. He was the acting director of the [[Owens Valley Radio Observatory]] from 1980–1981.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rochus E. (Robbie) Vogt|website=Caltech The Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy|url=http://pma.caltech.edu/people/rochus-e-robbie-vogt}}</ref> He was a mentor to [[Michael Turner (cosmologist)|Michael Turner]], [[Neil Gehrels]], and [[Anneila Sargent]].<ref name=breakthrough.caltech/> Gehrels was one of Vogt's doctoral students.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rochus E. (Robbie) Vogt|website=Physics Tree|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=187904}}</ref>

Vogt was a principal investigator of the [[Cosmic Ray Subsystem]] experiment of the [[Voyager mission]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/images/pia21122-voyagers-first-science-meeting/ |title=Voyager's First Science Meeting |website=[[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] }}</ref><ref>{{citation |url=https://calteches.library.caltech.edu/591/2/Vogt.pdf |title=Caltech's Vogt |first=JS |last=Dietrich |year=1984}}</ref>

{{blockquote|Vogt received the NASA Exceptional Scientific Achievement Medal for his work as a principal investigator on the [[Voyager program|Voyager mission]], and was chief scientist at Caltech’s [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] in 1977–78. He led the construction of Caltech’s Owens Valley Radio Observatory’s mm-wave interferometer, had a lead role in bringing about the [[Keck Observatory]] on Mauna Kea, Hawaii, and served as vice chair of the board of directors of the California Association for Research in Astronomy. From 1987 to 1994 he served as the director and principal investigator of the Caltech-MIT [[LIGO|Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory]] project, becoming a co-recipient of the 2016 Special Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics.<ref name=AlumniAward/>}}

In 1992, he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Historic Fellows|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic}}</ref>

Vogt married in 1958 and is the father of two daughters.
